draft.title: Epidemics and public health
card: An epidemic is a sudden rise in cases of a disease in a community or region. A pandemic is an epidemic that spreads across many countries.
keeps apart people who may have been exposed but are not yet known to be sick. Isolation separates people who are known to be infected.
handwashing, safe food handling and treated drinking water block the routes a pathogen uses to pass between people.
tracking cases shows where and how fast a disease is spreading. Contact tracing finds people who were near a case so they can be warned and tested.
draft.remember: Public health cuts the routes of spread and finds cases early, so an outbreak stays small.

a.q: Which action is an example of contact tracing?
opts: Finding and notifying people who spent time near a case
Keeping a confirmed case in a separate room at home
Treating a town's drinking water with chlorine
Counting the total number of new cases each week
a.why: Contact tracing means finding people who were near an infected person so they can be warned and tested. Counting cases is tracking, which shows how a disease is spreading but does not find the individual contacts.
a.clue: This action looks for people, not for numbers.

b.q: After an outbreak of a waterborne disease in a village, health workers treat the water supply and teach handwashing. How does this slow the outbreak?
opts: It blocks the routes the pathogen uses to spread
It makes people who are already infected recover faster
It finds everyone who was near an infected person
It separates people who may have been exposed
b.why: Treated water and handwashing stop the pathogen passing from person to person, so fewer new people are infected. Finding contacts and separating exposed people are different actions, and neither is described here.
b.clue: Think about what clean water and handwashing do to the pathogen's path.

a.best: Finding and notifying people who spent time near a case

b.best: It blocks the routes the pathogen uses to spread
